title: Warm rolling induced TRIP-to-TWIP transition in a metastable austenitic steel: Roles of grain boundary segregation, dislocations and nanoprecipitates
abstract: Tailoring the activation of transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) and twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) effects is critical for designing austenitic steels that combine high strength with excellent ductility. Here, we reported a transition in the dominant deformation mechanism from TRIP to TWIP in a metastable austenitic steel induced by warm rolling, leading to significantly-enhanced strength and more than a twofold increase in ductility. Comprehensive microstructural characterization and theoretical analysis reveal that warm rolling introduces pronounced carbon segregation at austenite grain boundaries, a high density of dislocations and nanoscale precipitates. The carbon enrichment substantially raises the local stacking fault energy, effectively suppressing ε-martensite formation. Meanwhile, the dense dislocation network provides abundant sites for stacking fault generation via dislocation dissociation, thereby promoting stacking fault and deformation twin formation. While the nanoprecipitates contribute moderately to strengthening, they increase slip resistance and further facilitate stacking fault formation under sufficiently-high applied stress. These findings highlight the role of warm rolling in precise manipulation of local chemistry and defect structures to control deformation mechanisms, offering a promising strategy to design strong and ductile austenitic steels for broad structural applications.
